h1: How a Restaurant Can Fill Weekdays and Turn First Visits into Regulars
quickAnswer: In this benchmark scenario, a two-outlet restaurant spends ₹40,000 a month on radius-targeted Instagram Reels with a weekday first-visit offer redeemed on WhatsApp. It tracks 520 first visits a month at ₹77 each — about ₹3.38 lakh in sales, an 8.5x return — and repeat customers rise from 18% to 27%.
cardSummary: 520 tracked first visits a month from Instagram, and repeat customers up from 18% to 27% in 90 days.

businessPattern.type: Two outlets, dine-in plus delivery apps, regional menu
businessPattern.location: Residential and IT-corridor neighbourhoods of a metro city
businessPattern.salesCycle: Same day — decisions made within hours

challenge: "Weekends are full, weekdays are empty, and delivery apps take a big cut of every order." Social media was a feed of dish photos with no offer, no tracking and no way to bring customers back. Google Maps listings had old photos and wrong weekday hours.
objectives: Fill weekday lunch and dinner slots with trackable first visits
Turn first-time diners into regulars without relying on discounts
Move a share of delivery orders from aggregators to direct ordering

whatWeDid.title: In-house food shoot
whatWeDid.body: One shoot day produced 12 Reels: dishes being made, the kitchen team, weekday combos. Real food and real people, no stock images.

whatWeDid.title: Radius-targeted Meta ads
whatWeDid.body: Reels shown to people within 4 km of each outlet, with a weekday-only first-visit offer redeemed by showing a WhatsApp message at the counter.

whatWeDid.title: Google Maps clean-up
whatWeDid.body: Correct hours for each outlet, full menu, weekly photo uploads and a reply to every review.

whatWeDid.title: WhatsApp loyalty loop
whatWeDid.body: Diners who redeemed the offer were opted in to a WhatsApp list: a birthday treat, new-dish alerts, and a direct-order link with no aggregator commission.

whatWeDid.title: Weekly read-out
whatWeDid.body: Redemptions counted by outlet and day, so budget moved to the outlet and slot with the lowest cost per visit.

rows: Modelled from profile completeness and weekly activity
Tracked first visits from ads / month
Indian Meta CPC ₹8–25 (OwlClaw) and restaurant search conversion rate ~8% (LocaliQ, US data)
Modelled effect of the WhatsApp loyalty loop

whatMadeTheDifference: Tracking. Once every first visit was counted through a WhatsApp redemption, the restaurant could see which outlet, day and creative paid back — and stop paying for the rest. The WhatsApp list also turned one-off diners into a channel the restaurant owns.

faqs.question: How can a restaurant increase footfall on weekdays?
faqs.answer: Run short Reels ads to people within a few kilometres, with a weekday-only offer that is easy to redeem and track. Keep Google Maps hours, menu and photos current so nearby searchers pick you.

faqs.question: How do you track footfall from Instagram ads?
faqs.answer: Use a redemption step — showing a WhatsApp message or code at the counter — and count redemptions by outlet and day. That turns ad spend into a cost per visit.

faqs.question: How can restaurants reduce dependence on delivery apps?
faqs.answer: Build a WhatsApp list of diners who opt in, and share a direct-ordering link with new-dish alerts and occasion offers. Every direct order avoids aggregator commission.

faqs.question: What return on ad spend can a restaurant expect?
faqs.answer: It varies by average bill and offer. In this scenario, a ₹650 average bill and ₹77 cost per visit give about 8.5x. Track it from your own redemptions.
